issues.description: Monkey-patching a private module attribute at import time complects this service with google-genai's internals
issues.detail: Setting `genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024` reaches into a private namespace from module top-level, so importing the LLM service mutates global SDK state for every consumer in the process. Three concerns are braided: our image feature, the SDK's transport tuning, and process-wide configuration. Pass a buffer size through a supported config path, or isolate the override behind an explicit opt-in.

issues.description: Image part handling complects decode, color-space assumption, and frame emission with no error path
issues.detail: `Image.open(io.BytesIO(part.inline_data.data))` followed by `image.tobytes()` with `format="RGB"` assumes the decoded mode is RGB. PNG with alpha, palette, or grayscale modes will silently emit mis-sized or mis-interpreted byte buffers downstream. Separate decode (value), mode-normalization (`.convert("RGB")`), and frame construction; let bad bytes raise rather than corrupt a frame.

issues.description: Default model change is a behavior flip braided into a feature PR
issues.detail: Flipping the default from `gemini-2.0-flash` to `gemini-2.5-flash` is an identity-over-time change for every existing caller who relied on the default. It is a separate decision from "add image support" and should be argued on its own merits, with a changelog entry that names the migration risk rather than tucking it under an image-generation feature.

issues.description: Image-model detection by substring match is incidental complexity hiding a missing capability concept
issues.detail: `if "image" in self._model_name` treats the model string as a flag carrier. The actual value being tested is "does this model support/require image output, and should thinking budget apply?" A small capability table keyed by model id (data, not string-sniffing) would make the rule explicit and survive the next model name that breaks the substring assumption.

issues.description: Image frames are emitted with no pairing to the text turn, complecting two response channels
issues.detail: Text parts go through the normal LLM text pipeline while image parts are push_frame'd inline with no correlation, ordering guarantee, or context-aggregator awareness. The assistant aggregator will record the text turn but not that an image was part of the same response. Decide explicitly what "the value of this turn" is when it contains both modalities, and make that relationship a first-class data shape rather than two side effects.

issues.description: Dependency specifiers jumped from `~=` pins to broad `>=x,<major` ranges without stating the tradeoff
issues.detail: Moving google-genai from `~=1.24.0` to `>=1.41.0,<2` (and the two cloud SDKs similarly) trades reproducibility for upgrade latitude. That may be the right call, but the PR does not say so. The decision deserves an explicit note: we are accepting that any future 1.x release lands in users' resolves without review.

review.summary: The image-generation feature is COMPLECTED with several unrelated concerns: a private-attribute monkey-patch on google-genai at import time, a silent default-model flip, and image emission whose decode/color-space/turn-coupling are all entangled in one elif branch. The essential complexity here is small (decode bytes, emit a frame); the incidental complexity (SDK internals, substring model detection, dual response channels with no correlation) is what the diff actually spends its budget on. Decompose: pull buffer config to a supported path, normalize image mode before tobytes, replace string-sniffing with a capability table, and split the default-model change into its own decision. The question that should have been asked first: what is the value of an LLM turn that returns both text and an image, and how does the rest of the pipeline see it as one fact rather than two side effects?
